question: Which is the largest country in the world by area?
detailedExplanation: Russia is the largest country in the world by area, covering about 17.1 million square kilometres - nearly twice the size of the next largest, Canada. China is the most populous country with India close behind.
subject: general-knowledge

question: The capital of Australia is:
detailedExplanation: Canberra is the capital of Australia, chosen as a compromise between Sydney and Melbourne. Sydney is the largest city, while Canberra was purpose-built as the seat of government.
subject: general-knowledge

question: What is the currency of Japan?
detailedExplanation: Japan's currency is the Yen (JPY). South Korea uses the Won, China uses the Yuan (Renminbi), and Vietnam uses the Dong.
subject: general-knowledge

question: The currency of Saudi Arabia is:
detailedExplanation: Saudi Arabia uses the Riyal (SAR). Qatar and Oman use the Riyal too, while Iran's currency is the Rial. Kuwait, Jordan, Iraq and Bahrain use the Dinar, and the UAE uses the Dirham.
subject: general-knowledge

question: Which is the longest river in the world?
detailedExplanation: The Nile, flowing about 6,650 km through northeastern Africa, is traditionally considered the longest river in the world. Some modern measurements suggest the Amazon is comparable or slightly longer, but the Nile remains the standard answer in competitive exams.
subject: general-knowledge

question: Mount Everest, the highest peak in the world, is situated in which range?
detailedExplanation: Mount Everest (8,849 m) is in the Himalayas on the Nepal-China (Tibet) border. It was first summited by Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay in 1953. K-2, the second highest, is in the Karakoram range.
subject: general-knowledge

question: The Sahara, the largest hot desert in the world, is located in:
detailedExplanation: The Sahara Desert spans about 9.2 million square kilometres across North Africa - nearly the size of the United States. Antarctica is the largest cold desert overall.
subject: general-knowledge

question: Which is the largest ocean of the world?
detailedExplanation: The Pacific Ocean is the largest and deepest ocean, covering about one-third of the Earth's surface. The Atlantic is second, the Indian third, and the Arctic is the smallest and shallowest.
subject: general-knowledge

question: The United Nations was established on:
detailedExplanation: The United Nations was established on 24 October 1945, when the UN Charter, signed in San Francisco on 26 June 1945, came into force. 24 October is celebrated as United Nations Day.
subject: general-knowledge

question: Which country has veto power in the UN Security Council?
detailedExplanation: The five permanent members of the UN Security Council - China, France, Russia, the United Kingdom and the United States - hold veto power. Germany, Japan and India are non-permanent elected members without veto power.
subject: general-knowledge

question: The headquarters of the World Bank is located in:
detailedExplanation: The World Bank and the International Monetary Fund (IMF) are both headquartered in Washington D.C., USA. The World Bank was established in 1944 at the Bretton Woods Conference, along with the IMF.
subject: general-knowledge

question: The headquarters of the World Trade Organization (WTO) is in:
detailedExplanation: The WTO, which replaced GATT in 1995, is headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland. Its Director-General has been Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala since 2021.
subject: general-knowledge

question: OPEC, the Organization of Petroleum Exporting Countries, has its headquarters in:
detailedExplanation: OPEC, founded in 1960 in Baghdad, has its headquarters in Vienna, Austria. Pakistan is not an OPEC member. Saudi Arabia is the largest oil producer within OPEC.
subject: general-knowledge

question: NATO was founded in 1949 primarily as:
detailedExplanation: NATO (North Atlantic Treaty Organization) was founded on 4 April 1949 as a collective defence military alliance of Western nations against the Soviet bloc. Its headquarters is in Brussels, Belgium.
subject: general-knowledge

question: The 'Old Trafford' cricket and football stadium is located in which city?
detailedExplanation: Old Trafford in Manchester, England, hosts both the historic cricket ground of Lancashire and the home ground of Manchester United football club.
subject: general-knowledge

question: Which country won the ICC Cricket World Cup 2023?
detailedExplanation: Australia won the ICC Cricket World Cup 2023, defeating India by six wickets in the final at Ahmedabad on 19 November 2023. It was Australia's sixth World Cup title.
subject: general-knowledge

question: The FIFA World Cup 2026 will be hosted by which countries?
detailedExplanation: The FIFA World Cup 2026 will be co-hosted by the United States, Mexico and Canada - the first 48-team World Cup. The final will be played at MetLife Stadium, New Jersey. The 2030 edition will be co-hosted by Spain, Portugal and Morocco.
subject: general-knowledge

question: The Olympic Games are held after every how many years?
detailedExplanation: The Summer Olympics are held every four years (the Olympic cycle), with the Winter Olympics alternating on a two-year offset. The first modern Olympics were held in Athens in 1896.
subject: general-knowledge

question: The national sport of Pakistan is:
detailedExplanation: Hockey is the national sport of Pakistan. Pakistan won Olympic gold in hockey in 1960, 1968 and 1984, and has won the Hockey World Cup four times - the most of any nation.
subject: general-knowledge

question: Which Pakistani squash player won the British Open a record ten times?
detailedExplanation: Jahangir Khan won the British Open ten times and the World Open six times. He also held an unbeaten run of 555 consecutive matches (1981-86). Jansher Khan won the World Open eight times.
subject: general-knowledge

question: Who was the first Pakistani to win the Nobel Prize?
detailedExplanation: Dr. Abdus Salam won the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1979 for his work on the electroweak theory, shared with Glashow and Weinberg. Malala Yousafzai won the Nobel Peace Prize in 2014.
subject: general-knowledge

question: Malala Yousafzai won the Nobel Peace Prize in 2014 at the age of:
detailedExplanation: Malala Yousafzai was 17 when she won the 2014 Nobel Peace Prize (shared with Kailash Satyarthi), becoming the youngest Nobel laureate in history. She was shot by militants in 2012 for advocating girls' education.
subject: general-knowledge

question: Nishan-e-Pakistan, the highest civilian award of Pakistan, was conferred upon which foreign head of state in 2019?
detailedExplanation: Saudi Arabia's Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman was awarded Nishan-e-Pakistan, Pakistan's highest civilian honour, during his visit to Pakistan in February 2019. The award recognizes extraordinary services to Pakistan.
subject: general-knowledge

question: Who invented the telephone?
detailedExplanation: Alexander Graham Bell patented the telephone in 1876. Thomas Edison invented the practical electric light bulb and phonograph; Marconi developed radio; and Tesla worked on alternating current systems.
subject: general-knowledge

question: Who is known as the father of modern computers?
detailedExplanation: Charles Babbage designed the Analytical Engine in the 1830s-40s, the first concept of a programmable general-purpose computer, earning him the title 'father of the computer'. Alan Turing is called the father of theoretical computer science and AI.
subject: general-knowledge

question: Who was the first human to step on the Moon?
detailedExplanation: Neil Armstrong stepped onto the Moon on 20 July 1969 during the Apollo 11 mission, famously saying: 'That's one small step for man, one giant leap for mankind.' Buzz Aldrin followed him; Michael Collins stayed in orbit.
subject: general-knowledge

question: The first human to travel into space was:
detailedExplanation: Yuri Gagarin of the USSR became the first human in space on 12 April 1961 aboard Vostok 1, completing one orbit of the Earth. Valentina Tereshkova was the first woman in space (1963).
subject: general-knowledge

question: 'The Prophet of Islam' is a book written by:
detailedExplanation: 'Seerat-un-Nabi' (The Prophet of Islam) was co-written by Allama Shibli Nomani and his student Syed Sulaiman Nadvi. Shibli died in 1914 before completing the series; Nadvi completed it in seven volumes.
subject: general-knowledge

question: Who wrote 'A Brief History of Time'?
detailedExplanation: Stephen Hawking published 'A Brief History of Time' in 1988. It explains cosmology, black holes and the big bang for general readers and became one of the best-selling science books of all time.
subject: general-knowledge

question: Who is the author of the national anthem of Bangladesh?
detailedExplanation: The national anthem of Bangladesh, 'Amar Shonar Bangla', was written and composed by Rabindranath Tagore in 1905. India's national anthem 'Jana Gana Mana' is also by Tagore.
subject: general-knowledge

question: What is the full form of 'UNESCO'?
optionA: United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization
optionB: United Nations Economic and Social Council Organization
optionC: United Nations Environmental Science and Conservation Organization
optionD: Universal Nations Education and Science Council
detailedExplanation: UNESCO stands for the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization, headquartered in Paris. It designates World Heritage Sites and promotes education, science and culture worldwide.
subject: general-knowledge

question: What does 'ASEAN' stand for?
optionA: Association of South East Asian Nations
optionB: Alliance of South East Asian Nations
optionC: Association of Southern European and Asian Nations
detailedExplanation: ASEAN - the Association of South East Asian Nations - was founded in 1967 in Bangkok with the founding members Indonesia, Malaysia, Philippines, Singapore and Thailand. Its secretariat is in Jakarta.
subject: general-knowledge

question: Which of the following is the largest delta in the world?
detailedExplanation: The Ganges-Brahmaputra Delta (Sundarbans) in Bangladesh and India is the largest delta in the world. The Sundarbans, shared with Bangladesh, is also the largest mangrove forest on Earth.
subject: general-knowledge

question: The 'Panama Canal' connects which two oceans?
detailedExplanation: The Panama Canal, opened in 1914 and expanded in 2016, connects the Atlantic Ocean (Caribbean Sea) with the Pacific Ocean across the Isthmus of Panama. The Suez Canal connects the Mediterranean with the Red Sea.
subject: general-knowledge

question: Which is the largest island in the world?
detailedExplanation: Greenland is the largest island in the world (about 2.16 million sq km). Australia is a continent rather than an island. Borneo is the largest island of Asia, and New Guinea the second largest island overall.
subject: general-knowledge

question: Which country is known as the 'Land of Rising Sun'?
detailedExplanation: Japan is called the 'Land of the Rising Sun' because of the Japanese name Nihon, meaning 'origin of the sun'. Its flag, the Hinomaru, shows a red sun.
subject: general-knowledge

question: Which country is called the 'Land of Thousand Lakes'?
detailedExplanation: Finland is called the 'Land of a Thousand Lakes' because it has over 180,000 lakes. Norway is the 'Land of Midnight Sun', and Pakistan's Hunza is called 'Shangri-La' - a term for paradise on earth.
subject: general-knowledge

question: The Great Wall of China was primarily built to:
optionB: Protect against invasions from the north
detailedExplanation: The Great Wall of China, stretching over 21,000 km, was built over centuries mainly to protect Chinese states and empires from invasions and raids by northern nomadic tribes such as the Mongols.
subject: general-knowledge

question: The Taj Mahal was built by which Mughal emperor?
detailedExplanation: Shah Jahan built the Taj Mahal in Agra between 1632 and 1653 in memory of his wife Mumtaz Mahal. It is one of the Seven Wonders of the World and a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
subject: general-knowledge

question: Which of the following is known as the 'City of Lights'?
detailedExplanation: Karachi is known as the 'City of Lights' (Roshniyon Ka Sheher) in Pakistan, while Paris is called the 'City of Light'. Lahore is known as the 'City of Gardens' and the 'Heart of Pakistan'.
subject: general-knowledge

question: The human body has how many pairs of chromosomes?
detailedExplanation: A normal human cell has 23 pairs of chromosomes - 22 pairs of autosomes and one pair of sex chromosomes - totalling 46. Females have XX and males have XY.
subject: general-knowledge

question: The deepest point of the world's oceans, the Mariana Trench, is located in which ocean?
detailedExplanation: The Mariana Trench in the western Pacific Ocean contains the Challenger Deep, the deepest known point on Earth at about 10,935 metres below sea level. It was first sounded by the HMS Challenger expedition.
subject: general-knowledge

question: Which organization awards the Nobel Prizes, established by Alfred Nobel's will?
optionB: Swedish Academy and Norwegian Nobel Committee
detailedExplanation: The Nobel Prizes were established by the will of Alfred Nobel (1895). Most prizes are awarded by institutions in Sweden (including the Swedish Academy for Literature), while the Peace Prize is awarded by the Norwegian Nobel Committee in Oslo.
subject: general-knowledge

question: Which country is the largest producer of tea in the world?
detailedExplanation: China is the world's largest producer of tea. India is the second largest producer and the largest consumer of tea in the world.
subject: general-knowledge

question: The International Red Cross was founded by:
detailedExplanation: Henry Dunant founded the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) in 1863 after witnessing the Battle of Solferino. He was awarded the first Nobel Peace Prize in 1901. The Red Crescent is used in Muslim countries including Pakistan.
subject: general-knowledge
